title: Understanding LASSO Regression
text: LASSO (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator) regression is a type of linear regression that uses shrinkage. Shrinkage is where data values are shrunk towards a central point, like the mean. The LASSO procedure encourages simple, sparse models (i.e., models with fewer parameters).

title: Effect of Lambda in LASSO
text: In LASSO regression, the parameter lambda (λ) controls the amount of shrinkage applied to the coefficients. A higher λ results in more shrinkage, which can lead to higher bias and lower variance.

title: Comparing Bias and Variance
text: Model A has a bias squared of $$2$$ and a variance of $$12$$, while Model B has a bias squared of $$4$$ and a variance of $$1$$. Consider how the bias and variance are affected by the value of λ in LASSO regression.

hintAnswer: Model B had a higher λ value.
title: Analyzing Model B
text: Given that Model B has a higher bias squared and lower variance compared to Model A, what can you infer about the λ value used in Model B?
choices: Model B had a higher λ value.
Model B had a lower λ value.
